reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) strongly supports the formation of M–N bonds, their role in suppressing metal dissolution, tuning adsorption energies, and enhancing durability in an N-doped HEA catalyst for ORR. However, all evidence comes from a single fuel cell study under very different conditions; there is no cited evidence that these mechanisms operate or confer benefits under automotive exhaust conditions with H2O, NO, and thermal aging, which is a key unsupported premise.
premises: Nitrogen doping forms multiple metal–nitrogen bonds (e.g., Ni–N, Co–N) in a Pt-rich HEA catalyst
M–N bonds suppress dissolution/oxidation of transition metals and inhibit Pt shell dissolution
N-doping tunes adsorption energies of intermediates, reducing poisoning by species like OH
N-induced lattice distortion slows metal diffusion, enhancing durability
These effects are transferable from fuel cell ORR conditions to automotive exhaust conditions with H2O, NO, and thermal aging
